accuracy.evidence: Layer names, order and features checked against the topic statement and standard primary sources (Royal Geographical Society rainforest structure; Encyclopaedia Britannica 'tropical rainforest'): forest floor dark and damp with fast leaf decay, understory of shade-tolerant small trees and shrubs, a continuous canopy roof holding most animal life, and scattered emergent trees above it. Animals use their typical teaching layer (leafcutter ants floor, tree frog understory, sloth and monkey canopy, harpy eagle emergent). Heights in items are framed as 'in one rainforest' with a 40 m canopy and 45–60 m emergents, within the usual 30–45 m and up to 60–70 m ranges.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips seen when children learn the layers: the canopy taken as the top layer, the understory and canopy swapped, the forest floor imagined as bright and hot, animals spread evenly or living mostly on the ground, and fallen leaves piling up for ever. Each is a prediction option, a placement message or a tagged challenge answer.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagrflayer stacks four bands of one forest in order, dims them for a climber that reports light at each height, drops leaves that rot into soil on the floor band, and places animals and plants by height. flagrfwhat builds a hot-wet climate near the Equator and flaganwhere matches animals to world habitats; neither is about levels inside one forest. Shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the order by building from the ground (wrong taps say 'start lower' or 'the canopy is the roof, but giant trees poke above it'); the dimming bands make 'dark floor, bright top' visible before the text states it; after placing five animals they see two badges in the canopy band, the most of any layer; and dropped leaves turn brown on the floor band.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option: 'the canopy' as the top, 'bright and sunny' for the floor, 'on the forest floor' for where most animals live, 'they stay there for ever' for leaves, and 'the canopy roof' for shade bushes. Each is disproved by the matching lab task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with big buttons; wrong answers are tagged top, flip, most, light, roof or order and each message names the slip: canopy is not the top, that is the other end, the floor has less food, the canopy is sunny, the roof is the canopy, the understory comes before the canopy.

readability.evidence: Kid text Flesch-Kincaid grade 2.8 (family target ≤ 5) with short sentences and a tall-house picture; key idea split into short sentences (grade 5.1); adult text 6.4 (≤ 10). Lab panel text is one or two short sentences per step, with emoji badges for animals and plants.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passed: no filler phrases and under 12% overlap with any lesson, including 577 What Is a Rainforest?. Kid paragraphs: the four names, the floor, understory and canopy, the emergent layer and the canopy-is-not-the-top trap. Adult: placement, why light and animals are distributed this way, mistakes, what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots of all six steps in both themes. The first pass put the sun over the step heading and a second caption over the note on the leaves step; the sun moved into the emergent band and the caption merged into the note. Animal and plant emoji now sit on outlined badges so they read against the canopy greens. Buttons use the 56 px young-learner size.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a big button: four layer-name buttons for building and for placing each animal and plant, Climb up / Climb down, and Drop a leaf, each with an aria-label. The canvas aria-label states the layer and its light after each move. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
